Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:8:1.hebrew: ואדם כיוצא בהן - כקרקעות, דבעי נמי תשע וכהן לשומו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:8:1.english: And a person is like them - Like land, as it also requires nine [judges] and a priest to appraise him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:10:1.english: An ox that is stoned - That gored a person and [the person] died.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:10:2.hebrew: כמיתת בעלים - אם היה נידון בחיוב מיתת בית דין, דבעי עשרים ושלשה — כך מיתת השור. דהאי בעליו יומת קרא יתירא להך דרשה, ולא דנתחייב קטלא, כדמפרש טעמא בגמ' (שם):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:10:2.english: As the death of the owner - If [the owner] were judged with liability of death by a court, which requires twenty-three [judges], so is the death of the ox [judged]. For this phrase, “its owner shall be put to death,” is a superfluous verse for this exposition, and not that he is [actually] liable to execution, as [the Gemara] explains the reason in the Gemara (there).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:10:3.hebrew: הזאב והארי כו' - שהמיתו אדם, ונידונין בסקילה כשור, דאמרינן בב"ק: "אחד שור ואחד כו'", בשור שנגח את הפרה (דף נד:):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:10:3.english: The wolf and the lion, etc. - [In a case] where they killed a person, and they are judged by stoning like an ox, as we say in Bava Kamma: “Whether an ox or [any other animal...],” in [the chapter entitled] Shor Shenagach Et HaParah (folio 54b).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:10:4.english: A cheetah - It is a wild animal.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:11:1.hebrew: ואין דנין לא את השבט - רובו של שבט שעבדו ע"ז במזיד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:11:1.english: And they judge neither a tribe - The majority of a tribe that worshiped idols intentionally.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:11:2.hebrew: נביא השקר - בחנק. בגמ' (דף טז.) בעי: מנלן דבעי שבעים ואחד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:11:2.english: A false prophet - [His execution is] by strangulation. In the Gemara (16a), it asks: From where do we [derive] that he requires seventy-one [judges]?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:11:3.hebrew: במלחמת הרשות - כל מלחמה קרי רשות, לבד ממלחמת יהושע, שהיתה לכבוש את ארץ ישראל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:11:3.english: In an optional war - [The Tanna] calls every war "optional," except for the war of Joshua, which was to conquer the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:11:5.hebrew: סנהדריות - שהיו מושיבים סנהדרי קטנה של כ"ג בכל עיר ועיר, כדכתיב (דברים ט״ז:י״ח) "תתן לך בכל שעריך", וצריכין בית דין הגדול שבלשכת הגזית לצאת ולהושיבם, וכו' יליף בגמ' (דף טז:):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:11:5.english: Sanhedrins - That they would establish a minor Sanhedrin of twenty-three in every city, as it is written (Deuteronomy 16:18): "You shall appoint for yourself in all your gates"; and the Great Court in the Chamber of Hewn Stone is required to go out and establish them, etc., as derived in the Gemara (16b).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:12:1.hebrew: בספר - כרך המבדיל בין ישראל לנכרים, ובלע"ז מרק"א. ובגמרא (שם) מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:12:1.english: On the frontier - A city that separates between Israel and the gentiles, and in Old French, marca [borderland]. And in the Gemara (there [16b]), it explains the reason.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:14:1.english: A congregation that judges - Ten [judges] who convict.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:14:2.hebrew: ועדה מצלת - עשרה מזכין. אשמעינן קרא דצריך עשרים, שאם יחלקו יהיו עשרה מחייבין ועשרה מזכין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:14:2.english: And a congregation that saves - Ten who acquit. The verse teaches us that twenty are required, so that if they disagree, there will be ten who convict and ten who acquit.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:15:1.english: To the evil congregation - It is written concerning the spies.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:16:1.hebrew: לרעות - אם הרוב מחייבין, לא תלך אחריהם להרוג:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:16:1.english: To convict - If the majority vote to convict, do not follow them to execute [him].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:16:2.hebrew: שומע אני - דלטובה, לזכות, הלך אחריהן, שאפי' מיעוט המזכים ורבים המחייבין, כתיב "לא תהיה אחרי רבים לרעות". אם כן, למה נאמר "אחרי רבים להטות"? משום זכות לא איצטריך ליה, אלא אפילו לחייב הלך אחריהן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:16:2.english: I would derive - That for good, [that is,] to acquit, follow them [the majority]; for even [when] those who acquit are a minority and those who convict are a majority, it is written: “You shall not follow a multitude to convict.” If so, why is it stated: “To incline after a multitude”? For [the sake of] acquittal it was not necessary [to state this]; rather, [it must mean that] even to convict, follow them [the majority].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:16:3.hebrew: לא כהטייתך - אחרי רבים לזכות, אני אומר לך לנטות אחרי רבים לחובה; אלא לזכות — על פי אחד, אפילו אין יתירין מזכין על המחייבין אלא אחד — זכה, אבל לחובה — עד שיהו מחייבין עודפין על המזכין שנים. והכי קאמר: "לא תהיה אחרי רבים לרעות" — על פי אחד, אבל "אחרי רבים" — בשנים, אפי' לרעות. הלכך, על כרחך כ"ב בעינן, דבציר מעשרה מזכין ליכא למימר, דהא כתיב "והצילו העדה", ותו לא משכחת חובה בציר מי"ב:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:16:3.english: Not like your inclination - Not like your inclination after a multitude to exonerate do I tell you to incline after a multitude to convict; rather, to exonerate is by a majority of one: even if those who exonerate do not exceed those who convict by more than one, he is exonerated. But to convict, it is not valid until those who convict exceed those who exonerate by two. And this is what the verse is saying: “You shall not follow after a multitude to convict” by a majority of one; but “after a multitude” by two, even to convict. Therefore, perforce we require twenty-two judges, for one cannot say that fewer than ten exonerate, since it is written: “And the congregation shall save,” and furthermore, you cannot find a verdict of conviction with fewer than twelve.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:1.hebrew: דיני ממונות בשלשה - בגמ' ילפינן להו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:1.english: Monetary cases [are adjudicated] by three - In the Gemara we derive them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:2.hebrew: גזילות - כופר בפקדון, דמששלח בו יד הוי גזלן. וכן החוטף מיד חבירו הוי גזלן, כגון: "ויגזול את החנית מיד המצרי" (שמואל ב כ״ג:כ״א). אבל לוה ולא שילם — לא מיקרי גזלן, דמלוה להוצאה ניתנה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:2.english: Robberies - [One who] denies [holding] a deposit, for once he misappropriated it, he becomes a robber; and likewise, one who snatches [something] from the hand of another is a robber, such as: “And he snatched the spear from the Egyptian’s hand” (II Samuel 23:21). But one who borrowed and did not repay is not called a robber, because a loan is given to be spent.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:3.hebrew: וחבלות - החובל בחבירו חייב בחמשה דברים, כדאמרינן בבבא קמא (דף פד.): ״ואיש כי יתן מום בעמיתו וגו' כן יעשה לו״ — בממון. ובגמ' פריך: היינו דיני ממונות:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:3.english: And personal injury - One who injures another is liable for five things, as we say in Bava Kamma (daf 84a): “And if a man cause a blemish in his neighbor... so shall it be done to him” — [meaning,] with money. And in the Gemara it asks: This is [the same as] monetary law!

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:4.hebrew: נזק - דשור המועד או אדם שהזיקו. ובגמ' פריך: היינו חבלות:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:4.english: Damage - [That] of a forewarned ox, or a person who caused damage. And in the Gemara it asks: Isn't this [the same as] personal injury?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:5.hebrew: תשלומי כפל - דגניבה שנמצא בידו, דכתיב (שמות כ״ב:ג׳) אם המצא תמצא בידו וגו':
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:5.english: Payment of double - For theft where [the stolen item] is found in his possession, as it is written (Exodus 22:3): “If the theft be found in his hand...”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:1:6.english: And fourfold and fivefold payments - [In the case] of an ox or a sheep that he slaughtered or sold.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:2:1.hebrew: האונס ומפתה - נערה בתולה, חמשים כסף:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:2:1.english: One who rapes and [one who] seduces - [In the case of] a virgin maiden, [he pays] fifty [shekels of] silver.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:2:2.hebrew: מוציא שם רע - לא מצאתי לבתך בתולים וגו', וענשו אותו מאה כסף וגו' (דברים כ״ב:י״ז):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:2:2.english: A defamer - [Concerning whom it says:] “I did not find tokens of virginity for your daughter,” etc., [and] “and they shall fine him one hundred [shekels of] silver,” etc. (Deuteronomy 22:17).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:3:1.hebrew: דיני נפשות - דאם אמת היה שזינתה תחתיו, היא בסקילה, ודיני נפשות בעינן כ"ג (לקמן בפירקין) (סנהדרין דף טו.):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:3:1.english: Capital law - For if it was true that she committed adultery while under him, she is [executed] by stoning, and [for] capital cases we require twenty-three [judges] (below in our chapter) (Sanhedrin 15a).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:4:1.hebrew: מכות - מלקות ארבעים. טעמא דר' ישמעאל ורבנן מפרש בגמרא (דף י.) מקראי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:4:1.english: Lashes - [The penalty of] forty lashes. The reasoning of Rabbi Yishmael and the Rabbis is explained in the Gemara (daf 10a) from verses.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:5:1.english: The intercalation of the month - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:5:2.hebrew: עיבור השנה - שהיו ב"ד יושבין ורואין אם צריכין לעבר מפני האביב והתקופה, כדאמרינן בגמרא. מילתיה דר' שמעון מיפרשא בגמרא בברייתא (דף י:):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:5:2.english: The intercalation of the year - That the court would sit and consider whether they need to intercalate [the year] on account of the spring [crop] and the equinox, as we say in the Gemara. The statement of Rabbi Shimon [ben Gamliel] is explained in the Gemara in a baraita (daf 10b).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:6:1.english: The laying of hands by the elders - [Performed] on the head of the bull [brought for] an unwitting communal sin.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:6:2.english: Ḥalitza [is performed] before three [judges] - In [tractate] Yevamot, [the Gemara] derives this in the chapter [entitled] Mitzvat Ḥalitza (Yevamot 101a).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:6:3.hebrew: מיאונין - יתומה קטנה שהשיאוה אמה ואחיה לדעתה, יוצאה בלא גט במיאון, כל זמן שלא גדלה תחתיו. ובשלשה בעינן — דכל דתקון רבנן, כעין דאורייתא תקון; ומיאונין דרבנן, דמדאורייתא אפילו מיאון לא בעיא, דאין קדושי קטנה כלום, אלא אם כן קדשה אביה, דכתיב (דברים כ״ב:ט״ז): "את בתי נתתי לאיש הזה":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:6:3.english: Refusal - An orphaned minor girl whom her mother and her brothers married off with her consent leaves [the marriage] without a bill of divorce through refusal, as long as she has not reached majority while living with him. And we require [a court of] three, for whatever the Rabbis instituted, they instituted modeled after Torah law; and refusal is rabbinic, since by Torah law she does not even require refusal, for the betrothal of a minor girl is of no validity unless her father betrothed her, as it is written (Deuteronomy 22:16): “I gave my daughter to this man.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:7:1.hebrew: נטע רבעי - אם בא לחללו על המעות, וכן מעשר שני:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:7:1.english: Fruit of a fourth-year sapling - If one comes to redeem it for money, and likewise [with] second tithe.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:7:2.hebrew: שאין דמיהן ידועין - כגון פירות והרקיבו, שאין להם שער בשוק:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:7:2.english: Where their value is not known - For example, produce that rotted, which has no [set] market price.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:7:3.hebrew: וההקדשות - הבא לפדותן, צריך שלשה לשומן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:7:3.english: And consecrated property - One who comes to redeem them requires three [people] to appraise them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:7:4.english: The valuations that are movable property - The Gemara explains [this] (daf 14b).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:7:5.hebrew: אחד מהם כהן - דכתיב כהן בפרשה: "כערכך הכהן" וגו' (ויקרא כז):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:7:5.english: One of them [must be] a priest - For "priest" is written in the passage: "As the priest values it..." (Leviticus 27).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:8:1.hebrew: והקרקעות - של הקדש, צריך ט' והעשירי כהן, לשומן אם בא לפדותן. בגמ' (דף טו.) מפרש ויליף להו מקראי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:8:1.english: And land - [That is,] of consecrated property: one requires nine [judges] and the tenth a priest, to appraise them if one comes to redeem them. In the Gemara (daf 15a), it explains and derives them from verses.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:8:2.hebrew: ואדם - הבא לפדות עצמו מיד הקדש, צריך עשרה לשומו. ובגמרא (שם) פריך: אדם מי קדיש:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:8:2.english: And a person - One who comes to redeem himself from the possession of the Temple treasury requires ten [judges] to appraise him. And in the Gemara (there), [the Gemara] asks: Can a person be consecrated?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:9:1.hebrew: דיני נפשות - דאם אמת היה שזינתה תחתיו, היא בסקילה, ודיני נפשות בעינן כ"ג (לקמן בפירקין) (סנהדרין דף טו.):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:9:1.english: Cases of capital law - For if it was true that she committed adultery while under his authority, she is [executed] by stoning, and for cases of capital law we require twenty-three [judges] (later in our chapter) (Sanhedrin 15a).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:9:2.hebrew: דיני נפשות - בעשרים ושלשה, לקמן יליף לה במתני':
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:9:2.english: Cases of capital law - [That they are judged] by twenty-three — [the Mishnah] derives it later in the Mishnah.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:9:3.hebrew: הרובע והנרבע - שור שרבע אשה, ובהמה שנרבעת לאיש — נידונית הבהמה ליסקל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:9:3.english: [An animal] that copulated and [an animal] that was copulated with - An ox that copulated with a woman, and an animal that was copulated with by a man — the animal is judged to be stoned.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:9:4.hebrew: בכ"ג - כאדם הרובע, דאיתקוש להדדי: והרגת את האשה ואת הבהמה — בהמה היינו רובע, ואיתקוש בהמה לאשה: מה אשה בכ"ג, אף בהמה בכ"ג:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:9:4.english: By twenty-three [judges] - [The animal that] copulated [is judged] like a human, for they are juxtaposed to each other: “And you shall kill the woman and the animal” (Leviticus 20:16) — the animal is [the one that] copulated, and the animal is juxtaposed to the woman: just as a woman [is judged] by twenty-three, so too an animal [is judged] by twenty-three.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 2a:9:5.english: And it states: “And you shall kill the animal” - [This verse] is written regarding an animal that was copulated with.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:7:1.hebrew: והברדלס - פ"ה: פוטיי"ש. ולא משמע כן, דאותו אינו עז כל כך, וכאן משמע שהוא עז ביותר ודרכו להמית את האדם. וכן בפרק אלו מציאות (ב"מ דף כד.) אמרי': "המציל מן הארי ומן הדוב כו'"; ובפ"ק דב"ק (טו: ושם) תנן: "הרי אלו מועדים". ואפשר שהוא מין נחש, דהא מפרש התם בגמ' (טז: ושם) דברדלס היינו אפא, וצבוע זהו אפא, וצבוע זהו אפעה, שהרי "גיא הצבועים" מתרגמינן "מישר אפעיא" (שמואל א יג), וכתיב: "אפעה ושרף מעופף" (ישעיהו ל׳:ו׳). ומיהו יש עדיין ברדלס אחר, דהא בפ"ק דבכורות (דף ח.) חשיב אפעה לע' שנה, ברדלס לג' שנים. ואע"ג דחשיב לה התם בהדי זאב וארי, ע"כ לאו היינו ההוא דהכא ודב"ק, דהא מפרש התם דהיינו אפא, דהוא אפעה. ויתכן דההוא דבכורות הוא פוטיי"ש, שפ"ה בכאן; וכן ההיא דפ"ק דפסחים (דף ט.): "אם חולדה וברדלס מצויין שם" — משמע שהיא חיה קטנה כעין חולדה:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:7:1.english: "And the bardelas" - The Commentary [Rashi] explained: Putois [polecat]. But [the context] does not indicate this, for that [creature] is not so ferocious, whereas here it implies that it is extremely ferocious and its nature is to kill human beings. And similarly, in the chapter [entitled] "Elu Metzi'ot" (Bava Metzia 24a), we say: "One who rescues [property] from a lion and from a bear, etc." [and the baraita lists the bardelas among them]; and in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (15b and there), we learned [in a mishna]: "These are forewarned" [and it lists the bardelas among deadly predators]. And it is possible that it is a type of serpent, for behold, there in the Gemara (16b and there) it explains that bardelas is afa, and tzevo'a [hyena] is afa, and tzevo'a is an ef'eh [viper], for "the Valley of Zeboim" is translated [in the Targum as] "the plain of vipers" (I Samuel 13[:18]), and it is written: "The viper and flying serpent" (Isaiah 30:6). However, there is still another [creature named] bardelas, for in the first chapter of Bekhorot (8a) it reckons [the gestation period of] a viper as seventy years, [and that of] a bardelas as three years. And even though it reckons it there alongside a wolf and a lion, perforce that is not the same one as here and [as in] Bava Kamma, for behold, there it explains that it is afa, which is an ef'eh [viper]. And it is likely that the one in Bekhorot is the putois [polecat] that the Commentary explained here; and similarly, that which [is taught in] the first chapter of Pesachim (9a): "If a weasel and a bardelas are commonly found there" — which implies that it is a small animal, similar to a weasel.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 2a:1:1.hebrew: דיני ממונות בשלשה - אחר ששנה דינים בתלתא בבי, משמיענו בכמה דנין אותם. הא דלא תנא כופר ושלשים של עבד, כדתנן שאר קנסות — י"מ משום דשור מיתתו בכ"ג, ובזמן שהשור בסקילה בעלים משלמין כופר ושלשים של עבד (ב"ק דף מג.), ודלא כר"א, דמחייב ע"פ עד אחד וע"פ הבעלים בפרק ארבעה וחמשה (שם מא:). ואין נראה, דהא איכא אמוראי התם דסברי, דאפי' ר' עקיבא דריש: "אם כופר", לרבות שלא בכוונה. ונראה לר"ת, דכופר ול' של עבד הוי בכלל חבלות. אי נמי: תנא ושייר הני, ושייר נמי יציאת עבד בראשי אברים, דקנסא הוא ובעי נמי ג' מומחין. וללישנא קמא, לא חשיב הא שייר, דאיכ' למימר דפשיטא ליה דהוי מכלל חבלות; אי נמי: התנא לא איירי אלא בממון הניתן מיד ליד:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 2a:1:1.english: Monetary cases [are decided] by three - After having taught the laws in the Three Gates [Bava Kamma, Bava Metzia, and Bava Batra], [the Tanna now] informs us with how many [judges] we adjudicate them. As for that which [the Tanna] did not teach kofer [the ransom payment for a person killed by an ox] and the thirty [sela] of a slave [Exodus 21:32], as he taught [other] penalties — some explain [that this is] because an ox's death [sentence] is [decided] by twenty-three [judges], and [only] when the ox is sentenced to stoning do the owners pay kofer and the thirty of a slave (Bava Kamma 43a); and [this explanation is] not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who obligates [payment of kofer even] based on the testimony of one witness or based on the owner's [own admission] in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Vachamishah (ibid. 41b). But [this explanation] does not appear [correct], for there are Amora'im there who maintain that even Rabbi Akiva expounds [the verse] "If ransom [be laid upon him]" (Exodus 21:30) to include [an ox that killed] unintentionally. And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that kofer and the thirty of a slave are included within [the category of] personal injury (chavalot). Alternatively, [the Tanna] taught [some cases] and omitted [others]: he omitted these, and he also omitted the emancipation of a slave through [the loss of] the tips of limbs [Exodus 21:26–27], which is a penalty and also requires three expert [judges]. And according to the first version, he does not consider this [emancipation] an omission, for one can say that it was obvious to him that it is part of [the category of] personal injury; alternatively, the Tanna was dealing only with monetary payments transferred from hand to hand.
